extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering dataset pairing real anonymized, aggregated Google search queries with Wikipedia pages, where annotators label long answers, short answers, or null.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.citeAs: Kwiatkowski, Tom, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, and Slav Petrov. 2019. "Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research." Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 7: 453–466. https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl_a_00276
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sampled from real anonymized, aggregated Google search queries using heuristics, filtered to those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results, and then human annotators labeled question-Wikipedia page pairs for question quality, long answers, and short answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples may have no answer labeled; both long and short answers can be NULL when no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages returned in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries were filtered using simple heuristics to retain questions of 8 words or more and only kept when a Wikipedia page appeared in the top 5 Google search results.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A single annotator completed three stages in succession: determine whether the question is good or bad, select the earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information for a long answer or mark no answer, and then select the short answer spans, yes/no, or no short answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated using post hoc expert consensus judgments and 25-way annotations to study variability and disagreement.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive research in natural language understanding and has utility to users through end-to-end question answering applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The choice to focus on Wikipedia may introduce biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on longer queries, excludes many non-questions and 'how to' questions, and is limited to Wikipedia as the evidence source.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and test benchmark for question answering research and evaluation of QA systems.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions (NQ), a new data set for QA research, along with methods for QA system evaluation.

description.evidence: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set. Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or marks null if no long/short answer is present.

inLanguage.evidence: All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more that have been issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or marks null if no long/short answer is present.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results. Annotation is performed using a custom annotation interface, by a pool of around 50 annotators, with an average annotation time of 80 seconds.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Both the long and short answer can be NULL if no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page. We consider the choice of whether or not to answer a question a core part of the question answering task, and do not discard the remaining 51% that have no answer labeled.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Source of questions The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more that have been issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time. From these queries, we sample a subset that either: 1. start with "who", "when", or "where" ... We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The guidelines and tooling divide the annotation task into three conceptual stages, where all three stages are completed by a single annotator in succession. Question Identification: Contributors determine whether the given question is good or bad. Long Answer Identification: For good questions only, annotators select the earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information for a reader to completely infer the answer to the question. Short Answer Identification: For examples with long answers, annotators select the entity or set of entities within the long answer that answer the question.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Annotation is performed using a custom annotation interface, by a pool of around 50 annotators, with an average annotation time of 80 seconds.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: This section describes evaluation of the quality of the human annotations in our data. We use a combination of two methods: 1) post hoc evaluation of correctness of non-null answers, under consensus judgments from four "experts"; 2) k-way annotations (with k = 25) on a subset of the data.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data. We also describe analysis of 25-way annotations on 302 examples, giving insights into human variability on the annotation task.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Part of speech tags and entities are identified using Google’s Cloud NLP API: https://cloud.google.com/natural-language.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Open-domain question answering (QA) is a benchmark task in natural language understanding (NLU), which has significant utility to users, and in addition is potentially a challenge task that can drive the development of methods for NLU.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We focus on Wikipedia as it is a very important source of factual information, and we believe that stylistically it is similar to other sources of factual information on the Web; however, like any data set there may be biases in this choice.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The goal of these heuristics is to discard a large proportion of queries that are non-questions, while retaining the majority of queries of 8 words or more in length that are questions. We focus on longer queries as they are more complex, and are thus a more challenging test for deep NLU. Future data collection efforts may introduce shorter queries, "how to" questions, or domains other than Wikipedia.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions (NQ), a new data set for QA research, along with methods for QA system evaluation. The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data.
